title: Whole organ sample embedding in potato starch suspension for ex vivo high field preclinical MRI
author: Elena Carlson
materials: Gather all materials within reach. Materials: Pre-assembled syringes + stir sticks, tweezers, potato starch, PBS, tissue tape, a sharpie, transfer pipette, a funnel, and tube rack stands.

For a MRI coil with (~20 mm diameter), add parafilm squares around the syringe and the zip ties, so that it fits snugly in the coil. This avoids motion artifacts during imaging. Approximately ~7 pairs of parafilm squares plus 2 zip ties, around this cat no. of syringe should be the correct size to fit snugly in the MRI coil.

steps.title: Prepare Workspace and Sample
steps.instruction: Prepare the work area and the organ sample for embedding.

substeps.instruction: Lay down paper towels, an absorbent pad, or use a tray to contain spills.
If the sample is in ethanol, transfer it to PBS briefly to rinse.
Dry the sample gently on absorbent paper towels using tweezers to avoid direct handling.

steps.title: Label and Verify Equipment
steps.instruction: Label the components and ensure the syringe assembly is functional.

substeps.instruction: Mark the sample ID clearly on the tube and syringe plunger using durable tape.
Inspect the glued stick-plunger assembly to verify the plunger moves smoothly within the barrel to prevent the syringe from getting stuck.

steps.title: Prepare Syringe Barrel
steps.instruction: Mark and prepare the syringe barrel for the starch suspension.

substeps.instruction: Mark the syringe barrel with arrows indicating brain orientation and location (e.g., 'rostral', 'caudal', 'jaw', 'top of skull/brain').
Tape the syringe tip (needle hub) lightly or add a syringe cap to prevent leaks.

steps.title: Prepare Potato Starch Suspension
steps.instruction: Create the starch suspension in the empty syringe barrel.

substeps.instruction: Determine the volume required based on the sample and stick; ensure there is at least enough dry potato starch to cover the volume taken up by the sample and stick (e.g., if the plunger seal is at 4 mL, add at least 4 mL of dry starch).
Using a funnel, add dry potato starch to the empty syringe barrel up to the mark corresponding to sample depth.
Use a transfer pipette to add PBS to reach a total volume of approximately 8 mL or more.
Cover the opening with parafilm and a thumb, then shake vigorously until the starch is fully dispersed with no clumps.

steps.title: Mount Sample to Plunger
steps.instruction: Secure the sample to the stick-plunger assembly.

substeps.instruction: Use a device (e.g., a test tube rack) to hold the syringe plunger and stick assembly steady.
Position the sample so major axes align with MRI planes (check alignment along stick for sagittal; rotate and verify by eye for axial and coronal).
Use a thin strip of 3M tape to hold the sample in place on the stick.

steps.title: Embed Sample in Starch
steps.instruction: Insert the sample into the suspension and pack the starch.

substeps.instruction: Verify the sample is secure by lifting and rotating the plunger/stick/sample assembly to ensure it does not fall off.
Flip the syringe so the opening faces up and the plunger is down; allow the potato starch to settle via gravity.
Remove the needle hub cap and carefully insert the plunger-stick-sample assembly into the syringe barrel.
Tap and rotate gently to release air bubbles around the sample; optionally use a shaker plate for stubborn bubbles.
Slowly push the PBS out from the top as the starch settles, being careful not to force the plunger too far or dislodge the sample.
Continue until the starch is densely packed around the sample and PBS is mostly removed from the top. (Optional: leave in the fridge overnight to let starch settle).

steps.title: Seal and Finalize Syringe
steps.instruction: Seal the assembly and add handles for the scanner.

substeps.instruction: Seal the plunger-syringe junction with hot glue.
Wrap the top of the syringe in parafilm or ceran wrap if a hub cap is unavailable.
Tape 2-4 zip ties to the syringe for easy handling in the scanner.

steps.title: MRI Positioning and Imaging
steps.instruction: Position the sample in the MRI scanner and optimize alignment.

substeps.instruction: Place the syringe in the head coil with the sample approximately centered.
Check scout images, then reposition and rotate the syringe/plunger to center the sample and align it 'flat' in the scanner view.

steps.title: Sample Recovery
steps.instruction: Remove the sample from the syringe after imaging.

substeps.instruction: Remove the sample from the MRI coil.
Remove all parafilm and zip ties.
Place a drain cover over the sink drain.
Place the syringe opening (needle hub end) under a running faucet and let the water force slowly push the plunger and sample out of the barrel.
